card.name: "in" before a patient population
card.fires_on: The word "in" (rarely "of") right after a drug name or a use/initiation phrase, where "patients" or "a patient" is expected next. Seen in warnings about using a product in certain patient groups.

modes.label: Drug name then "in"
modes.description: "in" follows a product name or the phrase "the use of" and leads into a patient group.
modes.example: The use of Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets<< in>> patients with acute or severe bronchial

modes.label: Initiated or used "in"
modes.description: "in" follows a verb like initiated or use and leads into a patient or a condition.
modes.example: If an opioid analgesic is initiated<< in>> a patient already taking a benzodiaz

card.plain: It marks the little word "in" that comes right before a patient group, such as "in patients with..." in a warning.
